vpc_topology_notes: Preferred topology: single-account VPC per environment (prod, staging), private subnets for inference nodes, public NAT/inspection in a central networking account.

Peering/Transit: prefer TGW + VPC attachments to central transit for cross-region connectivity; DR region = eu-west-1 but DATA RESIDENCY => primary workloads must not replicate PII to EU; DR only metadata and models encrypted with separate CMKs.
Inbound: customer will create VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) for Redwood control-plane talkbacks; no open inbound from internet to compute nodes.
Outbound: all egress through corporate NAT/inspection; allowlist required for Redwood management IP ranges during POC; full egress policy review required.
CIDR: they will provide /16 base; prefer Redwood to support configurability of subnets and security groups to match their NIST controls.
KMS integration: customer-managed CMK required; Redwood service needs wrapped/encrypted model artifacts and token encryption; HSM-backed key rotation policy required (rotate every 90 days).

Audit logging: must forward inference audit events (request id, model, token counts, timestamp, caller identity) to their Splunk via HTTPS collector or S3 bucket with retention 7 years; logs immutable and signed.
SAML/SSO: enterprise SSO required for console access, SCIM provisioning preferred for RBAC mapping.
architecture_risks_and_mitigations: Risk: egress restrictions block Redwood control-plane updates -> Mitigation: temporary allowlist window + VPN tunnel for bootstrap, then replace with PrivateLink endpoints.

Risk: customer CMK policies prevent Redwood from performing background key ops -> Mitigation: define a key policy with constrained encrypt/decrypt grants and use envelope encryption so Redwood never holds plaintext keys.
Risk: audit log schema mismatch with Splunk -> Mitigation: provide log schema mapping and a short adapter lambda as part of POC to translate events.
Risk: data residency ambiguous for backups -> Mitigation: explicit config flag to disable cross-region backups and store snapshots in US-only S3 buckets with account-level blocker.
